- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk premium or market panic.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 1.5σ above historical mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment index (0.1–0.3) into forecast adjustment, especially if sentiment >0.15.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.10, -0.20, +0.10), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment direction.
